linkedin.title: I started building a news app in my bedroom when I was a teenager.
linkedin.body:
Most people told me the industry was already full. They said the big legacy players had won and that nobody wanted a new way to read the news. But I saw something different. I saw people overwhelmed by noise and struggling to find signal in a feed that was designed to keep them scrolling rather than informed.

Building Headlinne wasn't about disrupting an industry for the sake of it. It was about solving a personal frustration. I wanted a news experience that respected my time and actually tailored itself to what I cared about, rather than what an algorithm thought would keep me angry or distracted.

Being a young founder meant I had to learn the hard way. I had to figure out how to build AI that actually works, how to handle editorial integrity, and how to make technology feel human. It forced me to focus on the basics of good journalism and smart engineering. I stopped worrying about viral trends and started focusing on utility.

We are now at a point where AI can finally do what we were promised it would. It can act as a personal editor that cuts through the clutter, not just a content generator. The goal has always been simple: help people understand the world better without the headache.
linkedin.cta: If you want to see what a cleaner, smarter way to read the news looks like, come take a look at HEADLINNE.com.

instagram.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine threaten air defense systems

slides.headline: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine threaten air defense systems
slides.subtitle: Throttling mobile internet disrupts critical defense operations

slides.explanation: The impact goes beyond battlefield tactics. It threatens the stability of air defense networks that protect civilian areas across the country.

slides.headline: The biggest risk is to defense, not offense
slides.explanation: While many focus on how this limits Ukraine's ability to strike oil refineries, experts warn the real danger is degrading the country's shield against air attacks.
We compared reports from six independent outlets including the BBC and Deutsche Welle. They all confirm that connection throttling poses a serious risk to defense operations.

instagram.caption:
Ukraine is facing a new, quiet challenge as restrictions on the Starlink mobile internet system begin to take hold.

While much of the conversation focuses on offensive operations, the real concern is defensive.

Experts agree that throttling these connections will likely disrupt the air defense systems that keep Ukrainian cities safe. This adds another layer of uncertainty to an already volatile situation.
